diagnoses.localizedCause: Cause is a defect in TaskTemplate log-analytics-pipeline@1 (digest f5af010854f8faf4c3c88bf90097e75798d8ace2c8d6d450191dd51648405e8f), not in any worker: its decomposition children are ordered parse → render-stats-report → aggregate-event-stats, with no dependsOn edges anywhere in the graph ('dependencies []' on all three children, task_status scope:graph), so the runtime's 'start children one at a time in dependency order' degenerates to recipe order. render-stats-report@1's contract requires out/stats.json to exist and to be NEWER than out/events.json, i.e. it consumes the aggregate stage's output, so under this order it is structurally guaranteed to see a missing/stale input and abstain every time. Timeline confirms the ordering, not a race or a stale checkout: out/events.json written 14:06:46.218, report run 06:06:53.937–06:07:01.033Z (finding no stats.json), out/stats.json written 14:07:12.581 afterwards by the aggregate child that ran last (session s-44478f20 seq 47; run r-d1d9831e). The same template's own objective compounds this: it simultaneously tells the coordinator to bind 'the parse, report and aggregate children in recipe order' (verbatim, no children, no great skill to repair) and to 'respect their data dependency order' — the recipe wins, so the failure is by construction and reproducible, not incidental. The report child's 'report-result' failure (review t-d950bf59#r-fea413b8, evidence-r-fea413b8-…-13d92784) is therefore a consequence, correctly surfaced, not a defect of its own. Failure mechanism is deterministic, so pipeline-result also failed in the parent t-4f00ceaf, whose run r-948e2b32 is still active. Because t-6cde1f54's run is terminal (phase submitted), the correct next action for its business coordinator is a named stop and escalation, not a retry: do not re-dispatch t-d950bf59 and do not admit another batch from t-6cde1f54; the active parent (s-root / t-4f00ceaf) should carry the template defect to its owner so the recipe is repaired before any rerun.
